run.change_description:
Update conn state to prevent concurrent connection attempts

Make callers of resetBackoff() lock the mutex

Add doc comment for resetTransportAndUnlock

Merge remote-tracking branch 'source/master' into fix_conn_connect_race

summary.intent: Hold `ac.mu` continuously across `addrConn.connect()`/`updateAddrs()` into the renamed `resetTransportAndUnlock()`, closing the unlock/re-lock window that let two goroutines both observe an idle addrConn and start parallel connection attempts (grpc/grpc-go#7365).
summary.issue_fit: Full. The diff implements exactly the fix arjan-bal described in issue #7365's root-cause comment (keep the lock held from the idle check through the state transition to Connecting), and the doc comment dfawley requested in review was added verbatim.
summary.coverage: The complete merge-base diff (1 file, +6/-7) was read; both call sites of the renamed lock-transfer helper (`connect()`, `updateAddrs()`) and their own callers (`balancer_wrapper.go`) were traced; a repo-wide search confirms no other caller of the retired `resetTransport` name remains.
check_details: Reviewer built (`go build .`) and vetted (`go vet .`) the package at the reviewed head: clean, no output.

Reviewer ran 5 related unit subtests under `-race` at the reviewed head (`Test/BackoffCancel`, `Test/ConnectParamsWithMinConnectTimeout`, `Test/Dial_OneBackoffPerRetryGroup`, `Test/ResetConnectBackoff`, `Test/UpdateAddresses_NoopIfCalledWithSameAddresses`): 5/5 pass.

Reviewer ran `Test/AuthorityRevive` (the flaky test named in issue #7365) under `-race`, 20 iterations at the reviewed head: 20/20 pass, 0 flakes, consistent with the author's reported 100000 flake-free local runs (not independently reproduced at that scale within the bounded run allowance).
Codecov (PR comment, accepted at the reviewed head) reports 100% patch coverage on the changed lines in clientconn.go; not independently rerun (no network access).

observations.fact: No new test was added or changed by this diff; the fix's correctness rests on the pre-existing (previously ~0.4% flaky) `Test/AuthorityRevive` integration test and the author's manual reruns, rather than a new deterministic unit test targeting the connect/updateAddrs race directly.
observations.evidence: The changed-file manifest shows only `clientconn.go` (+6/-7); `git log` for the range shows no test file touched. Reviewer independently reran `Test/AuthorityRevive` 20x under `-race` at the reviewed head with 0 failures.

observations.fact: Commit `6214c9dd1`'s message, "Make callers of resetBackoff() lock the mutex", does not describe its content: the commit changes the `connect()`/`updateAddrs()`/`resetTransport` locking handoff and does not touch the `resetBackoff` channel.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390/pr-body/"caller of resetTransport() keep holding the mutex instead of releasing it and having resetTransport() re-acquire it"
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go: `connect()` (formerly unlocking before calling `resetTransport()`) now falls straight into `resetTransportAndUnlock()` while still holding `ac.mu`; `updateAddrs()` likewise no longer unlocks before `go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock()`; and `resetTransportAndUnlock()` (renamed from `resetTransport`) no longer locks at entry, assuming the caller already holds `ac.mu`.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390/pr-body/"This ensures that no concurrent requests are able to start once caller of resetTransport does some validation and calls resetTransport"
requirements.evidence: Because `sync.Mutex` has no goroutine ownership, the lock acquired by `connect()`/`updateAddrs()` stays held (even when handed to a newly spawned goroutine) until `resetTransportAndUnlock()` itself sets state to `Connecting` and unlocks; no other caller can observe the addrConn as idle in between, closing the TOCTOU window issue #7365 describes.

A repository-wide search (`git grep -n resetTransport`) confirms exactly two remaining callers of the renamed helper, `clientconn.go:922` (`connect`) and `clientconn.go:996` (`updateAddrs`), both updated to hold the lock across the call; no stray caller of the old unlocked pattern remains.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390/pr-body/"Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts"
requirements.evidence: Reviewer ran `go test -race -run 'Test/AuthorityRevive$' -count=20 -v ./xds/internal/xdsclient/tests/` at head 76ef33f44a600c3ed1a385979fd1dfbcade3fbb6: 20/20 pass. Consistent with, though smaller in scale than, the author's reported 100000-run local verification, which is not independently reproducible within the bounded execution allowance.

clientconn.go:1231-1233 carries the doc comment `// resetTransportAndUnlock unconditionally connects the addrConn.` / `// ac.mu must be held by the caller, and this function will guarantee it is released.`, matching the text dfawley requested in review, added in commit ff977b39f.
